about: Mars in each of the twelve bhavas. Placements in 1, 4, 7, 8 and 12 are the classical Kuja (Mangal) dosha positions, handled separately as a yoga rule.

rules.says: Direct, physically forward and quick to act; the body carries marks, scars or a history of small accidents.
Earnings come from effort, land or a trade with an edge to it; speech cuts, and the mouth or teeth take the strain.
One of the strongest placements for nerve: competition is relished, hands are skilful, and rivals are simply outworked.
Friction at home and over property; gains in land are real but rarely arrive without a dispute first.
Learns fast and argues faster; matters of children carry strain, and speculation tends to end badly.
Mars is at its most useful here: opposition is dismantled, illness is fought off, and work with tools, blades or hard discipline agrees with the person.
Heat enters partnership: attraction is strong and so is contention, and business agreements need plain terms in writing.
Events arrive abruptly; surgery, inheritance disputes and a real appetite for getting to the bottom of things all belong here.
Convictions are defended rather than discussed; often friction with the father or with inherited doctrine.
A career built by force of work: engineering, surgery, uniforms, or anything where decisions must be made quickly and then carried out.
rules.note: The 10th is also Mars's own quarter of the chart, so it acts here at full strength.

rules.says: Income answers to effort directly, and ambition is met; elder siblings or seniors are a source of both help and rivalry.
Anger goes underground, where it costs more; losses follow impulse, and opposition is the kind that is not seen coming.
